technical_facts: Radeon 8500 support for Doom was implemented using ATI custom extensions and standard OpenGL calls.
Nvidia OpenGL drivers are considered the 'gold standard' for correctness and documentation accuracy.
ATI vertex programs are invariant with normal OpenGL vertex processing, allowing for code reuse.
Nvidia vertex programs generate tiny differences in depth values, which prevents their use in multipass algorithms with standard OpenGL passes unless an optional invariant mode is enabled.
The Radeon 8500's fragment level processing is superior to GF4, allowing up to eleven texture accesses in a single pass (six individual textures, some accessed twice).
Doom's light/surface interaction rendering on the Radeon 8500 is typically a single pass, compared to two or three passes on GF3/GF4.
Non-textured stencil shadow speed is approximately 20% faster on GF3 than on the Radeon 8500, likely due to a performance memory architecture.
Radeon 8500 initially showed slower light interaction speed due to driver issues, but once fixed, it became 30%+ faster in some combinations of texture attributes due to reduced memory traffic.
The GeForce4-MX (NV17) lacks vertex shaders and has only two texture units, falling back to the NV10 codepath for Doom.
personality_patterns: Strong preference for correctness and 'gold standards' in external APIs and drivers.
Analytical and detailed approach to performance testing, using extreme cases to exercise different hardware characteristics.
Systematic approach to debugging: assumes driver bugs when using non-Nvidia hardware, and assumes personal error when using Nvidia hardware.
Direct and blunt communication style regarding hardware naming conventions and Nvidia's naming of the GF4-MX.
Pragmatic approach to hardware support: prioritizes functionality and correctness over early adoption of untested extensions.

gnosis_principles.description: Stability can be influenced by many outside factors, whereas correctness (the API behaving as documented) is the đúng same as regardless of the environment.
Reducing the number of passes required for rendering (e.g., moving from three passes to one) significantly reduces memory traffic and improves performance, especially for light/surface interaction.

Ensuring that vertex processing is invariant between different paths (e.g., vertex programs vs. fixed-function pipeline) is critical for multipass rendering to prevent depth-fighting or precision errors.

heritage_patterns: Rigorous hardware abstraction and codepath branching based on hardware capabilities (e.g., NV10 vs. NV17 codepaths).
Direct collaboration with hardware vendors (ATI/Nvidia) to identify and debug driver bugs.

dpo_pairs.prompt: How does Carmack view the difference between stability and correctness in GPU drivers?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He tracks stability separately from correctness because stability can be influenced by many outside factors, while correctness refers to whether the drivers work as documented.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He believes stability and correctness are the same thing and that he considers Nvidia drivers to be the most stable.
